best_for: Creative thinkers who want to make games
not_for: Older teens looking for text-based coding
target_audience.who_should_take_foundation_first: This is a foundational course. No prior experience needed.

prerequisites.recommended: Imagination and a desire to tell stories.

system_requirements.software_accounts: A modern web browser and a free Scratch account.

overview.positioning: The perfect first step into the world of programming using fun, visual blocks.
overview.short_description: Dive into coding with Scratch! Snap colorful blocks together to build animations, interactive stories, and your very own playable games.

key_facts.ai_integration: None - Focuses purely on coding logic

why_now.industry_shift: Early coding education builds essential problem-solving skills.
why_now.ai_impact: Understanding logic helps kids grasp how digital systems work.
why_now.business_demand: Analytical thinking is crucial for the future workforce.
why_now.career_opportunity: Fosters confidence to pursue STEM subjects later.

learning_outcomes: NAVIGATE: Use the MIT Scratch interface with ease.
ANIMATE: Bring digital characters to life with movement and costumes.
PROGRAM: Apply loops, events, and conditionals logically.
CREATE: Design and publish complete interactive projects.

stages.focus: Learning the interface and making things move.
Adding rules, controls, and scoring to projects.
Designing a final game from scratch.

stages.name: Storyboarding
stages.desc: Deciding what the game will be about.

stages.name: Asset Creation
stages.desc: Picking or drawing sprites and backgrounds.

stages.name: Coding
stages.desc: Snapping blocks together to make it work.

best_practices: Always start scripts with an Event block (like the Green Flag).
Test your code frequently to make sure it does what you expect.
Use comments on your blocks to remember what they do.

common_mistakes.mistake: Sprites moving off the screen and getting lost.
common_mistakes.professional_approach: Always initialize your sprite's position (go to x, y) right under the Green Flag.

common_mistakes.mistake: Code executes instantly instead of waiting.
common_mistakes.professional_approach: Use 'wait 1 seconds' blocks between actions to control timing.

career_paths.employer_expectations: Basic understanding of cause and effect.

what_you_will_build: A chase game (e.g., Cat chasing a Mouse)
A final capstone project of the student's choice
final_deliverables: A public Scratch Studio featuring 4-5 completed projects.

assessment.criteria: Functionality, creativity, and use of required code blocks (loops, conditionals).

certification.title: Scratch Programming Certificate
certification.criteria: Complete and share the final game project.

next_learning_path.recommended_next: Young Coders Program or Python for Kids

faq.question: Does my child need to download anything?
faq.answer: No, Scratch runs entirely in the web browser.

faq.question: Can they share their games with friends?
faq.answer: Yes! Scratch allows you to share a link to your project so anyone can play it.

faq.question: What if they have never coded before?
faq.answer: That's perfectly fine. Scratch is designed specifically for absolute beginners.

modules.module_purpose: Familiarize students with the Scratch interface and basic sequencing.
what_you_will_learn: Adding and modifying sprites and backdrops

lessons.what_is_taught: The layout: Stage, Sprite panel, and Block palette.
lessons.why_it_matters: Knowing where things are is the first step to creating.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates an account and makes a sprite move 10 steps.

lessons.what_is_taught: Backdrops and Looks blocks (Say, Think, Costumes).
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates a digital greeting card with changing backgrounds and text.

lessons.what_is_taught: Green flag, key presses, and sprite clicking.
lessons.why_it_matters: Allows the user to interact with the program.
lessons.what_learner_does: Programs a sprite to jump when the spacebar is pressed.

modules.hands_on_practice: Build a short interactive story featuring two characters talking.
modules.assignment: Submit the interactive story project link.
modules.expected_outcome: Ability to create basic interactive animations.

modules.module_title: Game Logic: Loops, Conditionals, and Sensors
modules.module_purpose: Introduce the core concepts needed to turn animations into games.
what_you_will_learn: Using loops to repeat actions forever
Using Sensing blocks to detect collisions

lessons.why_it_matters: Essential for continuous game mechanics (like moving clouds).
Allows the game to enforce rules (e.g., if you touch lava, you lose).
lessons.what_learner_does: Programs keyboard controls (arrow keys) to move a character.

lessons.what_is_taught: Touching color and touching sprite blocks.
lessons.why_it_matters: Allows sprites to interact with each other.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a simple maze game where touching the walls sends you back.

modules.hands_on_practice: Create a 'Chase' game where one sprite must catch another.
modules.assignment: Submit the Chase game project link.
modules.expected_outcome: Understanding of how to build basic game rules.

modules.module_purpose: Add advanced features like scoring and complete a final capstone game.
what_you_will_learn: Creating and using Variables for scores
Planning and executing a complex project

lessons.what_learner_does: Adds a points system and a countdown timer to their Chase game.
lessons.expected_outcome: A game with win/loss states based on score.

lessons.why_it_matters: Allows multiple sprites to coordinate actions (like changing levels).
lessons.what_learner_does: Programs a 'Game Over' screen that appears when the timer hits zero.

lessons.why_it_matters: Develops confidence to build original ideas.
lessons.what_learner_does: Designs and codes an original game from start to finish.

modules.assignment: Submit the final project link and share it in the class studio.
modules.expected_outcome: Ability to independently design and program a full Scratch game.
